report:
Reviewed the complete precedence claim, all six implementation associations (expression checking, Scope, Resolver, Ribs, edition/scope helpers, and Symbol namespace/container operations), all nineteen substantive tests, and the explicit TODO test. This is an approval of the represented implementation and explicitly deferred remaining matrix, not a claim of complete Rust edition/macro-subnamespace support.

Lexical priority and path form: Resolver::resolve_path consults ribs for relative one-segment paths, with the receiver `self` special case; other paths traverse the requested module/container. Ribs searches innermost scopes and newest entries first, respecting Namespace. Expression blocks clone Scope and push/pop ribs; Scope uses body-global local allocation and an identity-keyed local type map, so allocations in nested or sibling scopes cannot shift another binding's type slot. Statement initialization precedes introducing the new binding. local_shadowing_does_not_change_qualified_lookup asserts parameter/local identities and crate-qualified function identity; nested_scope_shadowing_restores_the_outer_binding asserts inner bool, restored outer u16 and the later `after` binding's u16; sibling_scopes_do_not_share_bindings_or_local_type_slots asserts distinct bool/u8 identities and restored outer u16. These would detect both leaked shadowing and the previous vector-index/local-ID mismatch.

Module, namespace and ancestry rules: normal resolution selects direct/named imports before globs, then extern prelude, edition-specific standard prelude and primitive language prelude. Intermediate path segments use Type namespace; final segments use the caller's namespace. Symbol::name defines namespace classification and Symbol::children limits container traversal to modules/enums. resolve_anchor handles self, super, crate and external roots. qualified_paths_select_the_named_module_scope asserts self, parent and root targets despite a lexical name collision; absolute_external_paths_bypass_a_shadowing_local_module asserts distinct local and external Ordering variants. type_value_and_macro_namespaces_are_independent verifies a same-spelled struct, function and bang macro through their typed/symbol observations and generated item. named_type_import_takes_precedence_over_the_standard_prelude asserts custom::Option. The four edition tests assert TryInto absent in 2018/present in 2021 and IntoFuture absent in 2021/present in 2024, including exact unresolved-trait diagnostics for negative cases. scope.rs chooses the respective standard prelude module.

Import behavior: direct_items_take_precedence_over_globs and explicit_imports_take_precedence_over_globs assert selected identities, including a renamed import. The in-flight (module,name,namespace) stack terminates cyclic lookup. transitive_cyclic_globs_resolve_a_value_definition asserts the transitive function identity; the associated lib test directly checks a resolved Item ADT and an unresolved Missing error through a cycle. competing_glob_definitions_remain_ambiguous_despite_equal_types asserts an unresolved symbol and exactly two candidates, protecting definition-based ambiguity independent of equal signatures.

Two real defects were reproduced and corrected during this review with coordinator authorization. First, enum_glob_import_resolves_a_variant failed with unexpected `unresolved name` for Selected because resolve_glob discarded nonmodules. It now dispatches modules through cycle-aware module lookup and enums through namespace-filtered container lookup; other kinds contribute nothing. Local Selected and external std::cmp::Ordering::Less regressions assert their exact variant identities. Second, repeated_glob_routes_to_one_definition_are_unambiguous failed with `ambiguous name: 2 candidates` for the same crate::origin::value reached through two reexports. resolve_name_from_module now deduplicates by Symbol identity after selecting its precedence bucket, retaining first encounter order. The regression asserts one origin identity, while the distinct-definition ambiguity test still passes. This does not combine higher and lower precedence buckets.

The semantic_spec::todo::resolution_lookup_precedence entry remains explicitly deferred for the macro subnamespace matrix and Rust 2015 path rules. Closing those gaps requires fixtures for attribute/derive/bang distinctions and edition-specific legacy path/import behavior, with corresponding implementation work where unsupported; the empty TODO body supplies no executable evidence for those cases. It was narrowed only to remove the two now-implemented and tested cases, not relabeled as complete. No N/A entries exist. Existing coverage establishes modern-edition ordinary lookup and the listed namespace scenarios, not those deferred cases.

Verification actually executed: the two new focused regression commands each failed behaviorally before their fixes (the enum regression with unresolved name, the repeated-route regression with two-candidate ambiguity). After fixes, `cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test lookup_precedence` passed all 18 tests, including local/external enums, repeated-route identity and genuine ambiguity; `cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib transitive_local_globs_resolve_and_glob_cycles_terminate` passed its one selected test. `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo build` completed successfully, with existing warnings. No snapshot expectations or diagnostic annotations were weakened. Source helpers were captured through review read; compile_test executes independent rustc and Sage preparation before observation assertions. Coordinator will run centralized delegated post-codegen and Sage sanity checks for the modified files. Fresh start followed all implementation/test edits, and this report addresses the fresh inputs.
